summary: Same pattern — random sparks over a slowly-drifting field of coloured beams/diamond tiles, with matching beam widths, lit-pixel budget and dial set — but the port's sparks are rendered wrong (dim and random-hued instead of full-brightness and single-hued with white flecks), its base cycle runs ~9% slow, it never lands the original's exact 45 s repeat, and two dials (VerticalSweep, Speed) respond differently.
observations: Rig: grid 16x16 (256 px) by default. Both sides compile and run clean over 240 s; no runtime errors, no black/frozen frames on either side (zeroMotionFrames 1/2400 at 20 fps for both). Steady state at t=200-230 s is indistinguishable from t=0-30 s on both sides (orig mean 34 / motion 33, port mean 31 / motion 21 in both windows) — neither side decays, saturates or freezes.

Shared structure (verified phase-matched at 48x48 and 32x32): both draw a field of large coloured beams / tilted diamond tiles that drifts and re-orients, punctuated by isolated one-pixel sparks, with a ~9 s bright/dark breathing cycle. Beam-width distributions over a 54 s window at 48x48 are close: orig mean horizontal run 8.1 px (p50 5, p90 17), port 7.6 px (p50 5, p90 14); lit fraction 28.1% vs 26.0%; frames containing beams 31/50 on both.

PERIOD (decisive, measured by autocorrelation of meanBrightness over 120 s at 10/20/40 fps): original fundamental = 9.00 s exactly, with a 45.00 s super-cycle (autocorr 0.97 at 45 s vs 0.68-0.81 at 9/18/27/36 s). Port fundamental = 9.825 s, with only a weak 19.65 s doubling (0.99 at even multiples vs 0.96 at odd). Port is 9.2% SLOW on the base cycle.

Both sides are TIME-BASED, not frame-stepped: the same lags in SECONDS (450f@10fps = 900f@20fps = 1800f@40fps for the orig; 197f/393f/590f@10fps scaling likewise for the port) reproduce at every rate. No frame-rate coupling on either side.

LONG-TERM REPEAT: the original's whole beam field genuinely repeats — mean frame-to-frame pixel correlation jumps to 0.314 at exactly 45.0 s lag versus 0.03-0.05 at 9/18/27/36 s (the residual is the never-repeating sparks). The port never repeats: a lag scan of frame correlation from 2.45 s to 147 s peaks at only 0.161 (at 19.60 s) and is <0.07 everywhere else. So over a minute the original cycles through 5 distinguishable sub-cycles and comes back; the port's beam geometry keeps wandering.

SPARKS — original (n=426 isolated pixels sampled across 60 frames spanning 53 s): value p10/p50/p90 = 255/255/255, i.e. EVERY spark is full brightness and fully saturated; 8.9% are near-white (sat<0.15) 'hot' flecks; per-frame circular hue concentration R has median 1.00 (p10 0.45), i.e. within any one frame the coloured sparks nearly all share ONE hue, which drifts slowly over the cycle (pure red 255,0,x at t=0.15 s; yellow-green 12-39,255,0 at t=1-11 s; cyan later).

SPARKS — port (n=287 isolated pixels, same 60 frames): value p10/p50/p90 = 20/103/255, i.e. random brightness with a median of only ~40% of full; only 1.7% near-white; per-frame hue concentration R median 0.52 (p10 0.18), i.e. hues scattered around the wheel within a single frame. Visually: original = bright monochrome confetti with white flecks, port = dim multicoloured confetti.

Spark count and refresh rate DO match in character: both sides fully re-randomise the spark set every frame (at 40 fps, of ~20-30 lit sparks only 0-2 survive to the next frame on either side). Port draws ~33% fewer isolated sparks per frame (6.2 vs 9.3 at pinned dials over a 36 s window).

DYNAMIC RANGE: over 120 s at 20 fps the original's meanBrightness reaches max 116 while the port tops out at 72 (averages are close, 33.7 vs 30.9). The original hits near-full-frame saturation on its peaks; the port's brightest frames are ~1.6x dimmer.

MOTION: motion avg 32 (orig) vs 21 (port) at 20 fps over 120 s; motionLit 80.4 vs 38.9. Much of the gap is arithmetic — the port's sparks are ~2.5x dimmer so their per-frame re-randomisation contributes less diff (dark-frame motion 24.2 vs 17.9). But a phase-matched decorrelation check in the diamond-tile regime (orig at t=15.0 s, port at t=16.375 s = same phase given the 9.00/9.825 period ratio) shows the original reaching corr 0.37 after 0.10 s and the port only after ~0.20 s, so the port's beam field also drifts roughly 2x slower there at default dials.

COLOUR SPREAD: per-frame hue sweep across the 16-px width, measured over 60 frames spanning 53 s (phase-independent distribution): orig p10/p50/p90 = 0.14/0.29/0.79 of the hue wheel, port 0.23/0.45/1.05. The port's beams run about 1.5x more hue spread — where the original often shows a narrow two-colour blend (e.g. orange-yellow-green) the port shows most of a rainbow (blue-cyan-green-yellow-orange) across the same tile. Both are otherwise fully saturated (median sat 1.00); the port has 4.8% desaturated/white-cored pixels vs the original's 1.4%.

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH: the original exposes rgbPickerCenter (rgbPicker, label 'Center') and rgbPickerEdge (rgbPicker, label 'Edge'); the port exposes hsvPickerCenterBeamColor and hsvPickerEdgeBeamColor (hsvPicker, labels 'CenterBeamColor'/'EdgeBeamColor'). Different names AND different kinds — a saved control state will not transfer, and any UI that keys on the name/kind sees a different pattern. The five sliders (Width, Focus, Drive, Speed, VerticalSweep) match exactly in name and kind.

The two picker colours behave equivalently once dialled: with center=red / edge=blue both sides tint their beams red-to-blue; with center=green / edge=yellow both go green-to-yellow. Both sides also have phases of the cycle where the pickers are ignored and a fixed rainbow is drawn instead — that regime-gating matches.

Untouched defaults: both sides render the same look family untouched (dim red sparks at t=0, drifting to green/cyan/purple), and all headline numbers above were confirmed on the default 16x16 rig, so none of them are override-rig artefacts.

Seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give statistically identical output on both sides (orig mean 32 / motion 38-39, port mean 31 / motion 29 in every case) — the pattern is not seed-sensitive and no finding here rests on one seed.

The survey (60 s @ 5 fps and 240 s @ 2 fps) showed NO discrete mode regimes on either side — the rhythm images are continuous flicker with a repeating bright/dark breathing cycle rather than banded mode blocks. Regimes were therefore sampled as cycle phases: dark/spark-only (--skip 4, --skip 10), beam-onset, full-bright tile regime (--skip 15) and a late window (--skip 200).

dials.name: rgbPickerCenter / hsvPickerCenterBeamColor
dials.origEffect: rgbPicker named 'Center'. Sets the beam's inner colour; with center=(1,0,0) beams render red-cored, with center=(0,1,0) green-cored. Ignored during the pattern's fixed-rainbow phases.
dials.portEffect: hsvPicker named 'CenterBeamColor' — DIFFERENT NAME AND KIND. Effect equivalent once given all three HSV components (h=0 -> red core, h=0.333 -> green core), and it is ignored in the same rainbow phases.

dials.name: rgbPickerEdge / hsvPickerEdgeBeamColor
dials.origEffect: rgbPicker named 'Edge'. Sets the beam's outer colour; center=red/edge=blue gives red-to-blue beams.
dials.portEffect: hsvPicker named 'EdgeBeamColor' — DIFFERENT NAME AND KIND. Same visible effect (h=0.667 -> blue outer edge).

dials.name: sliderWidth
dials.origEffect: Widens and brightens the beams. With the other four sliders pinned at 0.5, meanBrightness over an 8 s window goes 35.9 (0) -> 41.6 (0.5) -> 45.2 (1); mean |W0-W1| pixel diff over 40 frames spanning 43 s = 16.7. Total lit fraction stays ~36% — Width redistributes/thickens rather than adding coverage.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and comparable magnitude (mean |W0-W1| = 15.3), but the port's coverage climbs with the dial (lit fraction 24.9% -> 31.6% -> 30.9% at 32x32) rather than staying flat, and the port's beams stay a little thinner throughout (mean run 6.6-7.1 px vs the original's 8.5 px at every setting).

dials.name: sliderFocus
dials.origEffect: Strongest brightness dial. Over a 20 s window meanBrightness 25 (0) -> 40 (1); at 0 the beams are largely absent and only sparks remain, at 1 the beams are bright and dominate. Probe maxDelta 9.17 / maxDeltaLit 44.11.
dials.portEffect: Same character (beams absent at 0, dominant at 1) but a stronger response: meanBrightness 23 (0) -> 49 (1), i.e. +113% vs the original's +60%. Probe maxDelta 18.00 / maxDeltaLit 47.45.

dials.name: sliderDrive
dials.origEffect: Effectively inert in the rendered output. Over a 36 s window with all other sliders pinned, Drive 0 / 0.5 / 1 give identical spark statistics (9.3 isolated sparks/frame, mean spark value 245-248, lit 36.0% at every setting) and the weakest probe delta of any control (0.91 / 4.38). Dial effect largely unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: Also effectively inert (6.2 sparks/frame, mean value 119, lit 41.1% at every setting; probe 1.36 / 3.89). Drive=0 sits marginally below 0.5/1 in overall brightness (mean 35 vs 37) — the same near-nothing the original does.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Mild increase in churn. Over a 36 s window with the other sliders pinned, motion avg 37.1 (Speed 0) -> 42.3 (Speed 1), +14%; meanBrightness unchanged (45.6 -> 45.3). In individual short windows Speed can be completely phase-neutral: at t=15.0-15.75 s, Speed 0 and Speed 1 render BYTE-IDENTICAL frames on the original.
dials.portEffect: Much stronger: motion avg 21.7 -> 31.6 over the same 36 s window, +46% (~3x the original's sensitivity), and in the t=15.0-15.75 s window where the original is byte-identical the port's frames differ by a mean of 70.8/255 per channel, with its 0.1 s decorrelation dropping from 0.53 to 0.08. Same direction, roughly 3x too responsive.

dials.name: sliderVerticalSweep
dials.origEffect: Re-orients the beam bundle. At 0 the beams are broad diagonal/near-horizontal bands; at 1 they become narrow near-vertical rays converging toward the top of the grid. Measured on beam-heavy frames at 32x32 over 43 s, the horizontal/vertical gradient ratio moves 0.982 (VS 0) -> 1.103 (0.5) -> 1.134 (1); meanBrightness falls 37 -> 30 over a 20 s window; mean |VS0-VS1| pixel diff = 24.7.
dials.portEffect: Changes the picture but NOT the orientation. Same measurement gives 0.907 -> 0.907 -> 0.912 (flat to within 0.6%); meanBrightness is unchanged (31 -> 31) and the pixel diff is only half the original's (12.98). The port shifts beam positions/phase instead of tilting the bundle toward vertical.

feedback: SPARK BRIGHTNESS is the most visible gap. The original's sparks are ALL drawn at full value (max channel exactly 255, saturation 1.0) — measured p10=p50=p90=255 over 426 sparks spanning 53 s. The port draws them at random brightness with median max-channel 103 (p10 20, p90 255), so the pattern reads dim and muddy where the original reads like bright confetti. Draw every spark at full value.

SPARK HUE: the original gives every coloured spark in a frame THE SAME hue, and that hue drifts slowly over the ~9 s cycle (pure red at t=0.15 s, yellow-green 38,255,0 through t=1-11 s, cyan later). Per-frame circular hue concentration R = 1.00 median. The port randomises hue per spark (R median 0.52, p10 0.18) so each frame is multicoloured confetti. Pick one spark hue per frame from the cycle, not one per spark.

WHITE SPARKS: 8.9% of the original's sparks are pure white 255,255,255 'hot' flecks mixed in with the coloured ones. The port has only 1.7% near-white pixels and no distinct white spark class. Add the white-fleck minority.
SPARK COUNT: the port draws ~33% fewer isolated sparks per frame (6.2 vs 9.3 at pinned dials over 36 s). Raise the density by roughly half.

BASE CYCLE RATE: the original's breathing cycle is exactly 9.00 s; the port's is 9.825 s (measured by autocorrelation of meanBrightness at 10, 20 and 40 fps — both sides are time-based, so this is a real constant, not a frame-rate issue). Speed the port's master cycle up by a factor of 1.092.

LONG-PERIOD STRUCTURE: the original's beam field repeats EXACTLY every 45.00 s — five distinct 9 s sub-cycles then a return (frame-level self-correlation 0.314 at 45 s vs 0.03-0.05 at 9/18/27/36 s). The port has no exact repeat anywhere between 2.45 s and 147 s (best 0.161 at 19.60 s) and only a weak 2-sub-cycle envelope. Whatever multi-term driver produces the original's 5:1 super-cycle is missing or has incommensurate periods in the port.

sliderVerticalSweep should TILT the beam bundle, not just move it. On the original, going 0 -> 1 rotates broad diagonal bands into narrow near-vertical rays and moves the horizontal/vertical gradient ratio from 0.982 to 1.134 while dropping meanBrightness 37 -> 30. The port's ratio is pinned at 0.907-0.912 across the whole range and its brightness does not move at all. The dial is wired to something other than the beam angle.

sliderSpeed is about 3x too strong on the port: it raises motion by 46% (21.7 -> 31.6) where the original raises it 14% (37.1 -> 42.3) over the same 36 s window. Scale the port's Speed term down by roughly a third.

CONTROL SURFACE: the original's colour controls are rgbPickerCenter and rgbPickerEdge, both kind rgbPicker, labelled 'Center' and 'Edge'. The port exposes hsvPickerCenterBeamColor and hsvPickerEdgeBeamColor, kind hsvPicker, labelled 'CenterBeamColor'/'EdgeBeamColor'. The rendered effect is equivalent, but rename and re-kind them to match the original so saved control state and UI presentation line up.

BEAM HUE SPREAD: the port sweeps ~1.5x more hue across a beam than the original (per-frame hue span across the 16-px width, median 0.45 of the wheel vs 0.29; p90 1.05 vs 0.79). The original usually shows a narrow two-colour blend where the port shows most of a rainbow. Compress the hue ramp between the centre and edge colours.

PEAK BRIGHTNESS: the original's brightest frames reach meanBrightness 116 over 120 s; the port tops out at 72. Combined with the dim sparks the port's whole dynamic range is compressed — the peaks should saturate closer to a full-frame wash.

Nothing needs fixing in beam geometry or density: beam-width distributions (mean run 8.1 vs 7.6 px, p50 5 on both), lit fraction (28.1% vs 26.0%), beam-frame incidence (31/50 on both), fps-invariance, seed-independence and long-run stability all match. Don't refactor those while fixing the above.
